analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 at BMO Stadium on Saturday 28 November (5:30 pm PT), five days after Game 1; a draw goes to penalties. LAFC have struggled to turn pressure into goals under interim coach Xavi Tamarit (nine goals in six games since 1 October), while St. Louis were outshot 23-13 in their last league game. The site lists Sergi Palencia as banned, but a one-match ban would cover Game 1 only.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, with LAFC expected to score 1.8. LAFC are much stronger at home (9-4-4 against 3-7-7 away), but they still scored a club-low 52 in the league and nine in six games under Tamarit, so I lean a little lower.

corners.text: The site expects 11.0 corners with 7.2 for LAFC. I lean higher: LAFC won 12 corners at Seattle when they had most of the ball, and at home against a St. Louis side that conceded nine at Houston they should pin the visitors back for long spells.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. Palencia should be available again if his ban covers only Game 1, and I found nothing else on discipline or the referee, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 31.9 shots, with LAFC taking almost 22. That is very high, but LAFC took 24 at Seattle and St. Louis allowed 23 at Houston, so the number has support; I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. I lean slightly lower because LAFC's volume has not turned into accuracy (eight of 24 on target at Seattle) and St. Louis had one shot on target in their last game.
